turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
I didn't ask about the essay yet. Who decided to enter the zero, and did anyone speak to me first?
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone call me first?
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
I haven't said anything about a timestamp, Hale. Flattery isn't an answer. Who decided on the zero, and why did no one call me first?
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.
"Had to." Under which rule, Hale? And you still haven't told me whether anyone called me before the zero went in.
